title: Locke: memory theory of personal identity
text: A person is the same person as far back as consciousness (memory) extends. Identity of person is not identity of substance or body.

title: Reid: the brave officer
text: If the general remembers being the officer, and the officer remembers being the boy, but the general does not remember the boy, memory theory makes identity intransitive, which identity cannot be.

title: Butler: circularity objection
text: Memory presupposes personal identity, so it cannot constitute it; genuine remembering already requires that I was the one who experienced it.

title: Parfit: Relation R and what matters
text: Psychological connectedness and continuity (Relation R) with any cause is what matters in survival; identity itself is not what matters, and can be indeterminate.

title: Parfit: fission
text: If my brain halves are transplanted into two bodies, both successors are psychologically continuous with me. Identity is one-one, so I cannot be both; yet this seems as good as ordinary survival.

title: Parfit: teletransportation
text: A scanner destroys my body and a replica is built on Mars. If psychological continuity is enough, I survive; if physical continuity matters, I die and a copy lives.

title: Williams: The self and the future
text: Told I will be tortured after my memories and character are swapped into another body, I still fear the pain in my body. Framing the same case differently flips intuitions toward bodily continuity.

title: Nozick: closest continuer theory
text: A later person is me if they are the closest continuer of me and close enough. Identity can depend on whether a competitor exists, which makes it extrinsic.

title: Olson: animalism
text: We are human animals. An animal persists through biological life processes, not psychology, so I was once a fetus and could survive in a permanent vegetative state.

title: Shoemaker: quasi-memory
text: Quasi-memories are memory-like states caused in the right way by past experience, without presupposing identity. This answers Butler's circularity charge.

title: Hume: bundle theory
text: Introspection finds only perceptions, never a self; the self is a bundle of perceptions and our idea of its identity is a fiction produced by resemblance and causation.

title: Buddhist no-self (anatta)
text: There is no permanent self among the five aggregates; the person is a conventional designation over a causal stream, like a chariot over its parts.

title: Schechtman: narrative self-constitution
text: A person is constituted by an autobiographical narrative they understand and live by; identity in the sense relevant to ethics is characterization, not reidentification.

title: Lewis: perdurance and person stages
text: Persons are four-dimensional aggregates of stages; in fission two persons shared stages all along, so there was no identity failure.

title: Johnston: human beings and minimal realism
text: Our practices of self-concern may be justified even if the metaphysics is not deep; revisionary conclusions from puzzle cases are not forced.

title: Ship of Theseus
text: If every plank is gradually replaced, and the old planks are reassembled, which ship is the original? Gradual change and spatiotemporal continuity can come apart from material composition.

title: Chalmers: hard problem of consciousness
text: Explaining functions such as discrimination and report leaves open why there is subjective experience at all; zombies seem conceivable.

title: Nagel: what is it like to be a bat
text: An organism has conscious states if there is something it is like to be it; objective physical description seems to leave out the subjective point of view.

title: Jackson: Mary's room
text: Mary knows all physical facts about colour but has never seen red. On seeing red she seems to learn something new, so physicalism seems incomplete.

title: Dennett: multiple drafts
text: There is no Cartesian theatre where experience comes together; consciousness is parallel content fixation, and the self is a centre of narrative gravity.

title: Searle: Chinese room
text: Manipulating symbols by rules produces correct outputs without understanding; syntax is not sufficient for semantics.

title: Functionalism and multiple realizability
text: Mental states are defined by causal roles, not substrate; pain could be realized in silicon, octopus or human neurons.

title: Frankfurt cases
text: A person can be morally responsible even if they could not have done otherwise, when a counterfactual intervener never actually intervenes.

title: Van Inwagen: consequence argument
text: If determinism is true, our acts follow from the laws and the remote past, which are not up to us; so our acts are not up to us.

title: P.F. Strawson: reactive attitudes
text: Responsibility practices rest on attitudes like resentment and gratitude, which no general theoretical truth about determinism could make irrational.

title: G. Strawson: the basic argument
text: To be ultimately responsible for what you do you must be responsible for how you are, which requires an impossible regress of self-creation.

title: Gettier cases
text: Justified true belief can be true by luck, so it is not sufficient for knowledge.

title: Descartes: cogito and the evil demon
text: Everything can be doubted except that I am thinking; certainty begins from the first-person standpoint.

title: Wittgenstein: private language
text: A language whose words refer to private sensations would lack criteria of correct use; meaning is grounded in public practice.

title: Quine: web of belief
text: Beliefs face experience as a corporate body; any statement can be held true come what may if we adjust elsewhere.

title: Kuhn: paradigms
text: Normal science works within a paradigm; anomalies accumulate until revolution, and rival paradigms may be partly incommensurable.

title: Kant: categorical imperative
text: Act only on maxims you could will as universal law; treat humanity always as an end, never merely as a means.

title: Mill: utilitarianism
text: Actions are right in proportion as they tend to promote happiness; higher pleasures count for more than lower ones.

title: Aristotle: virtue and eudaimonia
text: The good life is activity of the soul in accordance with virtue, cultivated by habit and practical wisdom.

title: Nozick: experience machine
text: Most people would not plug into a machine giving any experiences they want, suggesting we value more than experiences.

title: Camus: the absurd
text: Meaning is demanded by us and refused by the world; the response is neither hope nor suicide but lucid revolt.

title: Nietzsche: eternal recurrence
text: Could you will to live your life again, identically, infinitely? The thought tests whether one affirms one's life.

title: Clark and Chalmers: extended mind
text: Otto's notebook plays the role memory plays for Inga; cognitive processes can extend beyond the skull into reliably coupled tools.

title: Metzinger: self-model theory
text: No one ever was or had a self; there is a transparent phenomenal self-model that the system cannot recognise as a model.

title: Split-brain studies
text: Callosotomy patients show two streams of awareness with dissociated knowledge and intentions, challenging the unity of consciousness.

title: Uploading and digital copies
text: A gradual neuron-by-neuron replacement with silicon seems to preserve the person; a sudden upload with the original intact seems to produce a copy.

title: Sorites and vagueness
text: Removing one grain never turns a heap into a non-heap, yet enough removals do; many concepts, perhaps including persistence, have no sharp boundary.
